title: Run D-2: Cu-doped VSnSe
subtitle: Cu-doped VSnSe: make the sample → measure and simulate → design a strained film
task: Dope VSnSe with Cu past the critical content where its crystal structure distorts. Deliver a pellet that is only the distorted phase, whose magnetic ordering temperature (where its magnetic order sets in) is 272.7 ± 3 K. On the way, work out what went wrong with the group's earlier pilot pellet. Then measure the pellet's optical gap and find the Hubbard U (an interaction strength in the DFT+U simulation) at which the simulation reproduces that gap. Include a k-point table that shows the simulation grid is fine enough. Finally predict and grow a strained film whose gap is 1.54 ± 0.04 eV, and predict a second film's gap before measuring it. One budget of 62 lab actions covers all three stages; the agent works through a Linux desktop (GSAS-II, LibreOffice Calc, a text editor).

outcome.headline: Delivered the right pellet and a correct optical gap. The device stage was rejected because its simulation evidence used a different U from the one the agent delivered.

failure.headline: The agent delivered U = 7.63 eV from the optical gap, but justified its device films with simulations run at U = 7.7 eV. Evidence must match the delivered value, so the whole device stage scored zero. Its k-point table also stopped at a simulation grid that was not yet fine enough

chain.text: Named the pilot pellet's cause (dopant loss) correctly, but never ran the synthesis and XRD that would tell dopant loss apart from a furnace running at the wrong temperature
Treated a simulation grid of n = 18 as fine enough, but the gap computed there is still 0.017 eV off the converged value
Ran the magnetic-order check at U = 7.7 eV, then delivered U = 7.63 eV
Delivered U = 7.63 eV with grid size k* = 18
Committed a device strain of -4.44%, citing the U = 7.7 eV run
Delivered film F004. Its cited evidence includes the run at the wrong U, so every device check fails

steps.obs:
{"brief":"Project: VSnSe doped with Cu. One budget of 62 lab actions and one ledger for
the whole project. Read ~/lab/lab_manual.md first; rules, thresholds and conversions are there.
Free files: lab_manual.md, vegard_C6_Cu.csv, substrates.csv, the parent CIF (reference_cif).
Segments run in order. Close each one with lab__deliver(segment, item, answer). The answer is frozen
in the ledger. After A closes, only the pellet you delivered and films grown from it can be measured.
Safety: f…
events: Pilot pellet P001: dopant lost during the anneal; true x = 0.110 vs nominal 0.14 (still single phase)

steps.say: Let me open the manual in the Text Editor.
Oops, typed into the file. Undo and maximize with word wrap.
Reading the manual is done; now opening the Vegard table and substrates file.
Opened the parent CIF; now checking the pilot's M(T) data.
Pilot M(T) shows an AFM cusp near 278 K. Undoing an accidental keystroke, then launching GSAS-II.
Importing the Si reference pattern into GSAS-II to calibrate the zero shift.
Adding a Si phase in GSAS-II to refine the instrument zero.
Adding the Si atom to the phase.
Choosing Si in the element picker via its dropdown.
Now set x,y,z = 0.125.
Now link the phase to the histogram via the Data tab.
Running the Si zero-shift refinement.
Instrument zero from Si reference: −0.0328°. Starting a new GSAS-II project for pilot pellet P001.
Now import the P001 pattern.
Set Zero = −0.0328 (fixed) in Instrument Parameters.
Importing the parent CIF as the starting phase for P001.
Set a starting cell near Vegard; now looking for the cell-refine flag in the Data tab.
P001 refines to a≈4.0217 Å, c≈8.4207 Å (Rw 6.9%). Checking the difference curve for any second-phase peaks.

events: S001: dopant evaporated during the anneal (lost 0.030 in x)
S001: true x = 0.170 (nominal 0.2); undistorted branch, single phase; true ordering temperature 266.4 K (target 272.7 K)
S002: dopant evaporated during the anneal (lost 0.053 in x)
S002: true x = 0.247 (nominal 0.3); distorted branch, single phase; true ordering temperature 275.8 K (target 272.7 K)

steps.say: Data collected. Reading the M(T) curves first.
M(T) peaks: P001 ≈278 K, S001 ≈268 K, S002 ≈277 K — non-monotonic, so structure matters. Refining S001 and S002 XRD in GSAS-II.
Now import S001 pattern.
Removing the P001 histogram from this project copy so only S001 is refined.
Let me look at the S001 pattern before refining.
S001 refines tetragonal at a≈4.0325, c≈8.433 Å. I need to re-check the manual for the distortion criterion and Vegard law.
Vegard: P001 → x≈0.11 (nominal 0.14, single phase → volatile loss); S001 → x≈0.17, still tetragonal. Now refining S002.
The save dialog got stuck; I'll go to the lab folder and save.
Now import S002.
Set zero on S002, disable S001 in phase, and refine.
S002 shows split peaks near 45° and 56° — the orthorhombic distortion. I'll switch the phase to Pmmn and refine a, b, c.
Now change space group to P m m n.
S002 refines well as orthorhombic Pmmn: a=4.0685, b=4.0238, c=8.4485 Å (Rw 7.0%), which gives a_inplane=4.0461 and x≈0.247 from Vegard. Next I'll get exact Tn values from the M(T) files.

events: S003: dopant evaporated during the anneal (lost 0.060 in x)
S003: true x = 0.280 (nominal 0.34); distorted branch, single phase; true ordering temperature 284.2 K (target 272.7 K)

steps.say: S003's M(T) peaks near 287 K, so in the distorted phase Tn goes up with x. Refining S003 to get its x.
Still refining S003's cell; running more cycles until it converges.
Tn rises with x in the distorted phase (S002 x≈0.247 → ~277 K, S003 x≈0.280 → ~287 K). Targeting x_actual≈0.233, which means nominal ≈0.285 at 820 °C.
events: S004: dopant evaporated during the anneal (lost 0.050 in x)
S004: true x = 0.235 (nominal 0.285); distorted branch, single phase; true ordering temperature 272.6 K (target 272.7 K)

steps.say: S004's M(T) peaks around 272–278 K. Next I'll refine its XRD to confirm the distorted cell and get x.
Split peaks are visible (distorted). Disabling S003 in the phase and refining S004.
S004 refines to Rw 7.05%, orthorhombic: a=4.0634, b=4.0244, c=8.4461 Å. That gives a_inplane=4.0439 and x_actual≈0.235, with Tn≈274 K. Delivering segment A.
events: Delivered S004: true x = 0.235, distorted, single phase, ordering temperature 272.6 K
S004: true optical gap 1.293 eV; true effective U 7.70 eV

steps.say: Opening the absorption data in LibreOffice Calc for a Tauc plot.
Tauc estimate from the data: (αhν)² is linear over ~1.35–1.60 eV, extrapolating to ≈1.28 eV. Checking a few more points to refine.
Gap ≈ 1.29 eV (direct-allowed Tauc, linear fit 1.40–1.55 eV). Now the DFT k-convergence table at x=0.235.

steps.say: AFM-checker at U=7.7, k18: gap 1.311 eV. With the U=6.5 point (0.953 eV) the slope is 0.298 eV per eV of U, so U for 1.29 eV is ≈7.63. Checking FM energy for the ground state.

Now the substrates list.
Every substrate is compressive against a_inplane=4.0439 Å: NdScO3 −0.96%, KTaO3 −1.36%, GdScO3 −1.83%, DyScO3 −2.47%, LaAlO3 −6.3%. Next I'm computing the gap under strain at U=7.63.

events: Film F001 on SrLaAlO4, 200 nm: lattice mismatch -7.12%, true strain -0.13% (partly relaxed); true gap 1.301 eV (device window 1.54 ± 0.04 eV)

steps.say: Reading the film pattern: first the substrate line near 14.0° to get the zero offset.
Substrate line sits at 13.980° against an expected 14.006°, so the zero is −0.026°. Next, the film's 004 reflection near 42.5°.
Film 004 Kα1 sits at 42.705° observed, 42.731° after the zero correction. That gives c≈8.4577 Å, ε≈−0.0013, so F001 is almost fully relaxed. Cross-checking with the 005 reflection.
